title: Prior injury gave no clear repeated change in ozone and moisture slopes in four eastern US forest samples in 1995-2010
abstract: We tested whether the joint ozone and soil-moisture slope for recorded leaf injury differs with prior-year injury. We reused a public forest panel and kept consecutive visits in two eastern US regions and two periods. Four samples had 4,099 site-years. Models controlled site and year effects, weather, visit day and sampling effort. Prior-injury minus no-prior-injury slope differences ranged from -16.2 to +0.9 percentage points per 10 ppm-h W126 ozone times one moisture standard deviation. All four intervals included zero after correction for four tests. Before-visit exposures and closer monitors did not establish a repeated contrast. This does not show equal slopes. Short panels with prior injury can have dynamic bias. Missed injury, species turnover, exposure error and selected visits also limit inference. This is a new test on shared source records, not an independent archive or a causal climate effect. The package includes the exact input panel, code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes and a separate numerical check.

display.caption: The prior-injury minus no-prior-injury ozone by moisture slope contrast. Dark lines show marginal 95% intervals. Light lines show Bonferroni intervals for four tests. All four corrected intervals include zero.
Ozone by moisture slopes in the two prior-year injury groups. These are conditional linear projection slopes. They do not identify plant recovery or causal injury onset.
